caption:
24,000 jobs gone from six Indian IT majors in twelve months. That's the number moving through your WhatsApp today.

Here's what the spreadsheet doesn't show. When the list gets drawn up, competence is assumed. Everyone on that floor is competent. The question leadership actually answers is narrower: who can I picture in the next role.

That picture is built in meetings. How you enter a room. Whether your voice drops at the end of a sentence or climbs. Whether you fill silence or hold it. Whether your update sounds like a report or a decision.

In 35 years of command, I watched capable officers get passed over because they briefed like subordinates. The ones who advanced carried themselves like the rank above them before anyone handed it to them.

Your work is already good enough. Your bearing is doing the deciding.

topic.title: Six Indian IT majors shed 24,000 jobs in a year
topic.angle: A large share of India's overlooked mid-career managers sit inside these six firms or their client ecosystem, where the person who gets kept or poached isn't the most competent but the one leadership can picture in the next role.
topic.why_now: The Xpheno data via Economic Times hit the news cycle today (23 Oct 2026), giving a 48–72 hour window where '24,000 jobs' is the number in everyone's WhatsApp forwards.

rationale: A stark text-only visual carrying the news number lets the caption do the reframing without competing imagery, matching the brand's spare, authoritative register.
